fields.why: An ACIP recommendation report, but it presents its own evidence tables (trial efficacy with CIs, partly unpublished; a Monte Carlo benefit-risk model by age and risk group) and SCCS/VSD safety estimates, which goes beyond 'figures only cited ... to frame a recommendation'. B's 'limited' follows that clause literally, since most estimates come from prior presentations and studies.

A's only evidence for 'CDC surveillance system' is RSV-NET, which is the RSV analogue of COVID-NET/FluSurv-NET and so belongs under sentinel/network per the brief's common cases; no other CDC surveillance system is analyzed (VAERS is mentioned only as reporting guidance).

The Box names difficult 'transportation of patients ... for escalation of medical care' in remote or rural communities as the reason rural residence raises risk, i.e., a structural access determinant named as a cause, not a recommended action. A's null is defensible because the phrase sits inside a clinical eligibility criterion.

brief_issues: The 'limited' clause ('figures only cited from earlier reports to frame a recommendation') does not settle ACIP evidence-summary reports that tabulate many estimates (some unpublished) with CIs; a rule keyed on whether the report presents its own tables of estimates would decide it.
